items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1973-08-06
items.q: The man that first picked me up was Bernard Galway.

ctx.x: Yeah, you would deal with one man?

One man. How much territory? The man that first picked me up was Bernard Galway. And I had him, not only was his name, but Rabinowitz. And then finally this Al Travis that was the biggest crook in the world. And then the next biggest crook was this one that I picked up here, Chauncey Highland, on the revision of my band. Those were crooks. They weren't under bondage like the big companies are now. And the only major company that I went with that was under bonds was when I went to Joe Glazer. See, Glazer wanted me…

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1969-12-30
items.q: Goldberg bought all of that. And I wish it would have been possible that I could have stayed with him because I believe if Goldberg had stayed with us, it would have been feasible for him and profitable for all of us.

ctx.x: What about this Bernard Goldberg? Had you get in touch with him?

Well, Bernard Goldberg was an admirer of, he admired my playing and he thought that I would make a band leader. And he would come to Shadowland and he would ask me to organize a band. So I told him I wasn't ready. And when I came back here to New Orleans in, oh, it was 1929. But, Bernard came over and he said, why don't you get a band together? He says, I get you a real good job to start off with. I said, well, that sounds all right. He says, you need any money? He says, I'll give you a thousand dollars. So he…

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1961-06-06
items.q: through one of the bookers, the man that found me, Bernard Goldberg.

ctx.x: I remember seeing a picture of Duke Ellington wearing pants like that.

Well this was the style in those days. And this whole outfit was made by one of the best tailors in Dallas through one of the bookers, the man that found me, Bernard Goldberg. This other picture you see here is later on when I had stopped playing I was only featuring myself on two or three numbers. I had to take care of the business of the band. This was taken in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. And naturally this one here that you're looking at I was eight years old. This is in my backyard. You notice the wash tubs?…
That's a nice old style horn.

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1973-12-30
items.q: This was the only engagement that Bernard Goldberg had that was paying me enough money. And he could finance my band.

ctx.x: We were talking about the Dallas State Fair, how your band got started there. What went on at the Dallas State Fair? See, I never was at a...

Well, that's every October. That's a regular, one of the regular celebrations that they have. The world's fast stage fair. And this year, I don't remember what year it was that I was playing with. But it was in October of 1929. And the band that organized in New Orleans out there, Bernard Goldberg, had given me that money. We drove all the way from New Orleans, all the way from New Orleans into Dallas. And that was... Well, maybe I'll say that the Lord's blessed me more ways when one, it was... This was the only…
So you added men once the State Fair was over?
